title: Stage 2 & Stage 3 of Calving / Parturition
text:
Stage 2: Cervix becomes fully dilated and the calf moves through the birth canal.
Signs:
- Appearance of the water bag
- Abdominal contractions
- Calf's leg become visible
- Expulsion of the calf

[Image: Water bag]
Water bag

[Image: Calf's leg appeared at the vulva]
Calf's leg appeared at the vulva

Stage 3: Expulsion of the fetal membranes (8-12hrs).
Signs:
- Presence of placenta or fetal membrane.

facts: During Stage 2 of calving, the cervix becomes fully dilated.
During Stage 2 of calving, the calf moves through the birth canal.
Signs of Stage 2 of calving include the appearance of the water bag.
Signs of Stage 2 of calving include abdominal contractions.
Signs of Stage 2 of calving include the calf's leg becoming visible.
Signs of Stage 2 of calving culminate in the expulsion of the calf.
Stage 3 of calving is characterized by the expulsion of the fetal membranes.
Expulsion of fetal membranes in Stage 3 normally takes between 8 to 12 hours (8-12hrs).
A primary sign of Stage 3 of calving is the presence of the placenta or fetal membrane.
The document is part of the 'Dairysquare - Dairy Farming Module' on Page 43.
